title: Native prime-field factor-base size and decomposition-oracle tuning
status_note: Recommendation only; no experiment run or scheduled. Freeze the native baseline, executable protocol, costs and checker before dispatch.
question: Can joint selection of factor-base size and exact native decomposition oracle reduce complete one-target IC cost against the current verified prime-field incumbent on fresh matched workloads?
decision_value: A verified holdout reduction robust to the common native-operation pricing band promotes the selected recipe to the next IC baseline, even if rho is still cheaper. A null, failed or price-sensitive result retains the incumbent and narrows the tuning question; no coverage-only result is promoted to a pipeline improvement.

resources.notes: Proposed screening ceilings only; not estimates. Exact grid, cost derivation and caps must be frozen before ready. Existing native components are reused.

outputs.result_schema: Draft: sealed ecbench records, exclusive phase costs, complete native-counter inventory and independent replay receipts

cairn.notes: Not published or leased; draft only. No execution until the card is ready and a lab space is selected.

funding.rationale: Draft has no costed runnable protocol, so no queue priority or posted reward yet. A reviewer sets funding against the existing 131072-1000000 seed-card range when ready.
